text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Suleyman Demirel sends second letter to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan criticising him for the dismissal of national police chief.
- Erbakan goes on Moslem haj pilgrimage to Mecca with his whole family, including baby grandchildren.
- The governor of Nevsehir province objects to the military's decision to crack down on rising Islamist activism in a meeting held by interior ministry.
- A report presented by intelligence services to Erbakan reveals that Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels have 23 camps in neighbouring Iran.
- A proposal to announce an amnesty for 40,000 prisoners is not accepted in the ruling Islamist Welfare Party.
- International Monetary Fund (IMF) denies statements by Erbakan and his coalition partner Tansu Ciller's to the effect that a balanced budget has been achieved.
- Turkey seeking ways to overcome the embargo imposed on Iranian natural gas by the United States.
- World Trade Organisation says Turkey is among 21 countries with fastest growing trade volume.
